issues.body:
Re-verified at HEAD, unchanged since round 6.

Both `crates/sparq-shaclc/src/raw/shaclc12.rs` and `shaclc12ext.rs` open with `//! GENERATED by @rdf-shuttle/gen-rs from shaclc12ext.shuttle - DO NOT EDIT.` and this PR reformats both (~12.9k insertions / 4.0k deletions across the two).

`grep -niE 'fmt|rustfmt' scripts/regen-shuttle-parsers.sh` returns NOTHING. The script's own closing instruction is `now run: cargo test -p sparq-shaclc && cargo clippy -p sparq-shaclc --all-targets -- -D warnings` - it does not mention fmt. And `grep -c 'rustfmt::skip' crates/sparq-shaclc/src/raw/*.rs` returns 0 for both files, so the alternative escape hatch is not in place either.

So after this PR the checked-in artifacts are no longer byte-reproducible from the generator, and the first contributor who follows the documented procedure (`tests/provenance_drift.rs` literally instructs regenerate-don't-hand-edit) produces unformatted output that fails the now-hard `cargo fmt --all --check`.

It does not red today - provenance_drift.rs only pins the grammar SHA-256 and the DO-NOT-EDIT header, not artifact content - which is exactly why it will surface at the worst time. This PR is the one that creates the hazard, by flipping the gate.

`ignore = [...]` in rustfmt.toml is NOT an option: it is a nightly-only key, and rustfmt.toml documents a stable-options-only rule ('STABLE options only: cargo fmt on the stable toolchain rejects unstable keys').
issues.fix_hint:
Land one of these in this PR:

(a) PREFERRED - add a formatting step to `scripts/regen-shuttle-parsers.sh` after the artifacts are written, e.g. `cargo fmt -p sparq-shaclc` (or `rustfmt --edition 2021 crates/sparq-shaclc/src/raw/shaclc12.rs crates/sparq-shaclc/src/raw/shaclc12ext.rs`), so regeneration is fmt-clean by construction. While there, extend the script's closing `now run:` echo to name `cargo fmt --all --check` too.

(b) Alternatively revert the two `src/raw/*.rs` files to the generator's exact bytes and add a file-level `#![rustfmt::skip]` immediately under the `//!` header of each (tool attributes are stable), keeping them byte-identical to generator output and out of the gate.

(a) keeps the tree uniformly formatted and keeps the DO-NOT-EDIT contract truthful. Either way add one line to `tests/provenance_drift.rs` or the script header recording that generated artifacts must be fmt-clean.

I independently re-ran the mechanical audit this round (token-stream comparison of all 641 changed .rs files, comments stripped, `,{};` normalised, use/mod permutations factored out) and confirm the same small set of non-rustfmt-producible edits persists and nothing new joined it: this file, `crates/sparq-geo/tests/reproject.rs`, `crates/sparq-mcp/src/solid.rs`, `crates/sparq-conformance/src/inference/dl_suite.rs`. All four remain behaviour-preserving as far as I can verify (the test body and `want` array are byte-identical to main's, and nothing references the old name). So this is a reviewability/provenance defect, not a correctness one - but it is exactly the defect that matters in a 642-file diff whose whole reviewability rests on 'formatting only', and it is unaddressed after two rounds.
issues.fix_hint:
Either revert these four hunks so the diff is provably rustfmt-only, or state them explicitly in the PR body ('also renames <test>, moves <assert>, reformats <comment>') so reviewers and tooling know the token stream is not invariant.

This PR correctly rewrites the OpenSSF `warnings_strict` row to say the `fmt + clippy (gate)` job hard-gates `cargo fmt --all --check`. The sibling artifacts that the same gate-flip falsified are still wrong.

`grep -rniE 'fmt.*(non-blocking|informational|deferred|not gat)' --include='*.md' .` at HEAD returns THREE hits (round 6 asserted it returned exactly one - that claim was inaccurate):

- `compliance/ssdf/evidence.md:31` -> `| \`ci.yml#clippy\` | clippy \`-D warnings\` (gating) + fmt (non-blocking today) | PO.3.2, PW.5.1, PW.7.2 |`. False after this PR, and it makes the two compliance evidence files disagree about the same CI job.
- `.claude/agents/sparq-rust-feature.md:23` -> 'the workspace has an intentionally-deferred reformat (CI fmt is informational; clippy is the hard gate) ... do NOT run `cargo fmt`'.
- `.claude/agents/sparq-rust-impl.md:29` -> same guidance.

The two agent files are the operationally worse pair: they actively instruct implementers not to run `cargo fmt`, against a gate this PR makes hard-blocking. Every future contribution routed through them will red the new gate.

Separately, `bench/dict/README.md:87` still says 'The CI `clippy (gate) + fmt` job', a job name that no longer exists after this PR's rename. (`docs/branch-protection.md:77` WAS correctly updated - I confirmed it reads `fmt + clippy (gate)`.)

None of these four files is in the diff, so they are attached here to the openssf evidence file this PR did edit; they are the same doc-honesty drift, caused by this PR, and should land with it.

2. `.claude/agents/sparq-rust-feature.md:23` and `.claude/agents/sparq-rust-impl.md:29` - replace the deferred-reformat guidance with 'the workspace is fully rustfmt-formatted and `cargo fmt --all --check` is a hard CI gate; run `cargo fmt` before pushing'.

issues.body:
Re-verified: HEAD line 587 is `format!("method not found: {}", other),`; origin/main line 569 is `Err(RpcError::new(METHOD_NOT_FOUND, format!("method not found: {other}")))`. rustfmt performs this transformation in neither direction - it is a hand edit or an errant lint autofix.

Output is byte-identical, so there is no behaviour change, and it is not an immediate clippy-gate risk (the `format!("...{}", var)` shape already occurs widely across `crates/` and main is green under the workspace `-D warnings` gate, so `clippy::uninlined_format_args` is not firing on the CI toolchain). It is a latent inconsistency if that lint ever tightens, and it breaks the formatting-only claim for this file.

The correct rustfmt output for this hunk keeps the captured identifier.
issues.fix_hint:
Restore the captured-identifier form and let rustfmt wrap it:

```rust
other => Err(RpcError::new(
    METHOD_NOT_FOUND,
    format!("method not found: {other}"),
)),
```

This keeps the file's diff formatting-only and stays on the inlined-arg side the rest of the module uses.

issues.body:
Re-verified in the `lint:` job at HEAD. The job is renamed to `fmt + clippy (gate)`, but `- name: rustfmt (check)` is still the LAST step, after `clippy` (default features), `clippy --all-features`, both `cargo doc` passes, and the standalone bench/dict clippy + selftest.

`cargo fmt --all --check` requires no compilation and finishes in seconds. Running it last means a PR whose only defect is formatting burns the entire multi-build lint job before reporting - the most expensive possible way to surface the cheapest possible failure, on a gate that by construction of this PR will fire regularly while contributors (and the agent docs flagged above) adapt.
issues.fix_hint:
Move the step to be the first one after toolchain/cache setup, matching the `fmt + clippy (gate)` name:

```yaml
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@e18b497796c12c097a38f9edb9d0641fb99eee32 # v2
      - name: rustfmt (check)
        run: cargo fmt --all --check
      - name: clippy (deny warnings)
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

`rustup component add rustfmt clippy` already runs above it, so no other change is needed.

verdict.summary:
Round 7. I re-verified every round-6 finding against the checkout rather than trusting the record; all still stand, at the same severities. Nothing changed except one further merge from main (e6075353).

That merge is CLEAN, which is the one genuine improvement: merge-base is now origin/main exactly, so round 6's residual '10 files main changed post-branch-point were not reformatted' no longer exists. I re-ran the mechanical audit at token level over all 641 changed .rs files (comment-stripped, punctuation-normalised, use/mod permutations factored out) and hand-checked word-diffs on the soundness-critical surfaces (sparq-zk/verify.rs, sparq-zk-compose build/lib/join_gates, sparq-engine/exec.rs, sparq-server/http.rs + solid_authz.rs, sparq-substrate/join.rs, sparq-reason/dtype.rs, sparq-core/lib.rs): all pure rustfmt wrapping plus use/mod reordering. The new merge invented no new non-formatting content.

But the three round-6 majors are untouched:
(1) scripts/regen-shuttle-parsers.sh STILL has no fmt step (grep -iE 'fmt|rustfmt' returns nothing; its closing 'now run:' line names only cargo test + clippy), and neither reformatted DO-NOT-EDIT artifact carries #![rustfmt::skip] (0 matches). The next regeneration therefore reds the very gate this PR hardens.
(2) The four non-rustfmt edits are all still present: the sparq-engine test rename (HEAD 'total_order' vs main 'lenient_order' - still on neither merge parent), the reproject.rs statement move, the solid.rs un-inlined format arg, the dl_suite.rs comment reword.
(3) compliance/ssdf/evidence.md:31 still reads 'fmt (non-blocking today)'. My grep found TWO further stale claims round 6 missed: .claude/agents/sparq-rust-feature.md:23 and sparq-rust-impl.md:29 both still say 'CI fmt is informational' and instruct agents NOT to run cargo fmt.
